newsitem.title: UK: UK CBI says accepts rate rise in light of budget.
newsitem.headline: UK CBI says accepts rate rise in light of budget.

text.p: The Confederation of British Industry said on Thursday that a quarter-point interest rate rise was probably necessary after last week's budget.

"Business reluctantly accepts the need for this interest rate rise as last week's budget did not do enough to offset inflationary pressures from domestic demand growth," Adair Turner, director-general at the CBI, said in a statement.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown tightened fiscal policy by almost six billion pounds in his first budget but little of that was directed at the consumer.
The Bank of England's monetary policy committee announced a quarter-point base rate rise on Thursday, taking them to 6.75 percent, the third in three months.

"We would stress that further interest rate rises in the short-term would be unwelcome. The weakness of prospective EMU currencies and higher UK interest rates have pushed sterling up to have a severe impact on UK exporters," Turner said.
"The situation should not be exacerbated and is itself likely to slow growth over the next year."
Sterling actually fell more than a pfennig after Thursday's rate rise but is still up more than 20 percent in the last year, squeezing exporters in the process.
